newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Cool weekend for Brazil coffee but no problems.
newsitem.headline: Cool weekend for Brazil coffee but no problems.

text.p: Brazil's key coffee regions saw a cool weekend but temperatures stayed well above critical levels, cooperatives and meteorologists said Sunday.
In Pocos de Caldas, Minas Gerais state, traditionally the country's coldest coffee region, minimum temperatures over the weekend were eight degrees Celsius, the local cooperative said.

In Londrina, Parana, Brazil's most southern coffee producing state, early morning temperatures were also eight degrees Celsius on Saturday but had warmed to 10 degrees on Sunday, the cooperative said.
The cool temperatures are due to a polar air mass which has already left the country but which has brought a blanket of cold weather in its wake.
Temperatures should now begin to pick up again during the course of this week, said independent local meteorologists Somar.
"The worst is over," said Somar forecaster Marcio Custodio.
The next polar air mass is expected to arrive in the far south of the country during the weekend of June 7/8, Custodio said.
The country's coffee regions should first see rain on June 8/9 with temperatures falling from the early morning of June 10, Custodio said.
The air mass, currently in the Pacific Ocean, has a intensity of 1,022 millibars but is expected to get stronger.
Given it is likely to enter Brazil overland, it is worth following more closely than other air masses which come in from the sea, carrying humidity, Custodio said.
However a clearer indication of any threat to the coffee regions will only be known in the middle of this week, he added.
The world's coffee markets are watching the progress of Brazil's winter particularly closely this year given a background of low consumer stocks.
Expectations are that Brazil will see a larger coffee crop in 1998 but any frost this winter could dramatically change supply prospects.
